$comment: The upstream revisions this repository's ports are built against, in machine-readable form.
Every one of these checkouts is gitignored (see `.gitignore`: `.ref/`), so a CI runner starts
with none of them and must fetch the exact commit recorded here. That makes this file the
single place where 'which upstream' is answered, and it is what the scheduled drift check
(.github/workflows/check-upstream-drift.yml) diffs against the live remotes: if a branch has
moved past the commit below, an engine is out of date and only that engine needs rebuilding.
`engine` names the build workflow to dispatch for that checkout, and the key under `engines`
is the engine name used by ports/lib/fetch-engine.mjs. `full-clone` marks checkouts that
cannot be fetched shallowly: a shallow clone of vcpkg makes its own `read-tree` fail with
exit code 128 while resolving its baseline, so it must be a full clone.
EVERY KEY UNDER `engines` IS DISPATCHABLE, AND THAT IS WHY ARTEMIS IS NOT ONE OF THEM
check-drift.mjs does not consult `publish-gated` or any other flag: it iterates every key of
`engines` (line 114, `Object.entries(pins.engines)`), requires repository/branch/commit, and for
any engine whose pinned commit is no longer the branch head it pushes that engine's `workflow`
into the matrix the drift job fans out over -- which then runs `gh workflow run <that path>`.
So an `engines` entry is a promise that a workflow by that name exists, and it must be deleted
in the same commit that deletes the workflow.
The artemis-compat host build (a browser host patched onto the third-party sources, artifact
`artemis-web-android.wasm`) is retired, and with it `.github/workflows/build-wasm-artemis.yml`
and `.github/scripts/build-artemis.sh`. Leaving the entry behind would have made the daily
cron dispatch a workflow that no longer exists the next time artemis-compat moved.
The upstream pin itself is not lost -- it moved to `artemis-bridge` below, which is a SIBLING of
`engines` and therefore never iterated by the drift check. That asymmetry is the point: the
bridge still compiles code from `.ref/artemis-compat`, so it still needs the pin, but the
bridge is not an engine build and has no drift-dispatch contract. The pin is recorded in the
bridge workflow's own `upstream-repository` / `upstream-commit` inputs.
Do not edit `commit` by hand to silence the drift check. Moving a pin means rebuilding the
engine, re-running its gates, and publishing a new manifest -- the commit recorded here is
the one the published bytes were built from.

vcpkg.why: kirikiroid2-web/vcpkg-configuration.json pins this commit as its builtin-registry baseline, and a shallow clone cannot resolve it.

wabt.why: wasm2c regenerates the Artemis bridge's C source from the vendored SDK modules.

$comment: The bridge is not an engine build: it recompiles the official Artemis module from its
wasm2c-transpiled form on top of the hand-written engine in ports/artemis/src. Its only
input that is not tracked is the 103 MB transpile, and that is regenerable byte-for-byte,
so the workflow produces it instead of downloading it.
The md5 values are the reference transpiles' hashes, measured on this machine against
wabt at the commit above. They are recorded so the workflow can assert it regenerated the
same bytes rather than a merely-similar file: wasm2c derives the emitted
`#include "artemis.wasm2c.h"` from the `-o` basename, so any other output name yields a
file that differs by about 30 bytes and does not compile.
